subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Cavitation: Bubbles That Destroy
description: One-minute skill: Cavitation: Bubbles That Destroy.

hook.text: Tiny bubbles form in fast-moving water and collapse with violent force.

buildup.text: When pressure drops below vapor pressure, liquid boils into tiny bubbles.

discovery.text: Those bubbles collapse when pressure rises again, releasing shockwaves.

twist.text: Repeated shockwaves pit and erode even hardened steel surfaces.

climax.text: Pump impellers, ship propellers, and valves all suffer from cavitation.

punchline.text: The tiniest bubbles pack the biggest punch.

quiz.question: What causes cavitation damage?
options: Air enters the system and corrodes metal surfaces
Vapor bubbles collapse violently, sending shockwaves into nearby surfaces
High-speed liquid directly erodes the metal by friction
